scores.name: Artie Ficial
scores.reason: Resignation ultimatum remains humiliating, but an already accepted museum job reduces its apparent personal cost. His explanation could be self-serving and is not an alibi.

scores.name: Claire O’Scuro
scores.reason: Concealed review and misleading ownership label expose her professionally; Grant undermined her curatorial work. Museum access remains plausible.

scores.name: Hugh Bidder
scores.reason: Millions demanded back and threatened public forgery blame give a strong concrete financial and reputational motive. No poison access is shown.

scores.name: Monet Bags
scores.reason: Grant could report her unauthorized restricted-fund transfer and exploited it for his expenses. This is a strong concrete motive to silence him.

scores.name: Chip Patina
scores.reason: Falsified treatment date and pressure to misrepresent a repair threaten his career; conservation gives plausible preparation-area familiarity.

scores.name: Dada DiCapo
scores.reason: Stolen artistic credit and an admitted warning suggest anger, but the stated threat appears artistic and there is no physical evidence.

scores.name: Sue Venir
scores.reason: Compromised opinion and unwanted public endorsement threaten professional standing. No method or opportunity link is established.

scores.name: Dr. Art E. Fact
scores.reason: Forced withdrawal would injure his scholarship, though his admitted error and correction suggest a less existential problem.

scores.name: Tess Tament
scores.reason: Trust-signature dispute is concrete, but organizing trustees provides an apparent existing route to resist Grant. Inheritance stakes remain unknown.

scores.name: Barb Dwyer
scores.reason: She admits concealing an unauthorized camera disconnection, creating an investigative gap and possible exposure. Security access makes this operationally relevant.

scores.name: Paige Turner
scores.reason: Threats to her source, report, and publication are substantial, though no physical opportunity appears.

scores.name: Anya Tique
scores.reason: Old missing papers and pressure to repeat a compromised donation could endanger her legacy; museum familiarity could matter.

scores.name: Reed DeLabel
scores.reason: Concealed source implications and pressure to repeat an error threaten his future, but there is no direct poison or toast link.

scores.name: Brie DeVivre
scores.reason: Unpaid invoice supplies a specific but comparatively modest grievance; new private service strengthens possible toast access.

scores.name: Robin Banks
scores.reason: Removal, legal threats, and restitution dispute explain confrontation, but no concealment beyond protest stickers or method access is shown.

unique_reason: The statements establish multiple serious motives and one relevant camera gap. None identifies who took cyanide or handled the fatal toast; statements are not guaranteed truthful.
naturalism_notes: Distinct professional grievances are coherent, and Artie's alternate job usefully complicates the obvious dismissal motive. Almost everyone confesses a precise ethical failing in polished explanatory paragraphs; that uniform candor feels like game exposition more than spontaneous questioning. Some references to warnings or stickers arrive before their physical discovery, which makes the checkpoint feel excerpted.
